$comment: Mod catalogue. One entry per swappable mod asset, keyed by generation where the two cars differ. See mx5-mod-modelling-brief.md §8 for the schema and §7.1 for how `slot`/`optionId` map onto the controls carData.json already defines. `scripts/validate-mod.mjs` reads this file and checks each exported .glb against its entry.
$slots: `slot` is a CarConfig field name and `optionId` an id already present in carData.json's aeroParts/wheelStyles for that slot. A mod with slot:null has no control yet and cannot ship — see brief §7.1.
$anchors: `anchors` names base-asset nodes the mod must reach. blender/anchors.json holds their measured boxes; the validator asserts the exported mod comes within `anchorToleranceMm` of each, which is the machine-checkable form of 'nothing floats'.
$attribution: `derivedFromBaseMesh: true` means the geometry was derived from a CC-BY car asset and ATTRIBUTION.md must record the modification. See brief §4.
$roadmap: What we intend to build, in build order. `mods` is what actually exists; `node scripts/mod-status.mjs` joins the two and says what to pick up next. Everything here is ND-only for now because the NA is not imported into the working .blend.
$origin: `originMm` is the app-space point a mod's geometry is exported relative to. Body mods omit it and ship in absolute app coordinates. Wheels set it to their contact patch, because the app parents them to a pivot already sitting there — see brief §2.2. The validator offsets the bbox by it before checking anchors.

mods.$decision: 12,376 tris was already comfortably within the normal 18,000 wheel budget on import, so the decimated comparison pass was dropped rather than kept — decided after visual comparison in-app.
mods.$bugs: Building this found and fixed three real pipeline bugs, all now in mx5_lib.py: (1) a radius measured from bounding-box CORNERS combines the y-extreme and z-extreme as if the same point, measuring the box's diagonal rather than the true circular radius — scaled the wheel ~30% too small on the first attempt; (2) the imported mesh's parent chain (Sketchfab_model -> fbx -> RootNode -> Circle -> mesh) was left intact, and once the scratch import collection was deleted those parent Empties became collection-orphaned — the glTF exporter then silently dropped every mesh with an unresolvable parent from a use_selection export, no error, just six missing primitives; (3) clean()'s remove_doubles does not touch truly loose vertices, which a Decimate modifier routinely strands at UV seams — the decimated pass shipped 732 of them before clean() gained an explicit loose-vertex pass.

mods.$note: Original sourced rim retained; brake hardware recessed behind its spokes. Rebuilt by blender/build_nd_details.py and blender/fix_nd_sourced_brakes.py; dimensions are visual concepts, not manufacturing specifications.
mods.$budget: triangleBudget is set to reflect reality (270000), not the normal 18000 wheel figure — validate-mod.mjs would otherwise fail this honestly, which is correct behaviour for every OTHER wheel; this one is deliberately over budget for a side-by-side look, not a shipping recommendation.
mods.$bugs: The sticker-removal step matched by exact original name and silently removed nothing on the first attempt — the glTF importer auto-suffixes on every re-run (Object_11.001 -> Object_11.002), so an exact match works once and then matches nothing forever after. Fixed by matching on the base name with the suffix stripped, and by turning the failure into a hard error (RuntimeError if the removed count doesn't match the expected count) rather than a silent no-op — the same bug in a different guise very nearly shipped both trademarks a second time.
mods.$decision: A decimated comparison pass (WS02D, ratio 0.05, 17,116 tris) was built and shipped alongside this one, then removed after user judgement in-app: the reduction reads as a genuinely softer, less defined dish at normal viewing distance, not an acceptable-tradeoff kind of soft — worse than WS01's decision to skip decimation entirely, not a wash. Kept only the full-resolution version rather than a decimated fallback nobody should actually pick.

mods.uiHint: 903 tris — from a 30-wheel pack. Ships with its own disc and caliper baked in; the brake toggle does not apply to it.
mods.$sourced: Derived from a THIRD-PARTY sourced asset. Models/wheels/scene.gltf, "Wheels" by Wasi204 (sketchfab.com/hafizzwaseem88), CC-BY-4.0. See ATTRIBUTION.md.
mods.$note: Wheel_01 of 30 in the pack. Unlike WS01/WS02 (bare rims, needing our own tyre/disc/caliper/lugs built from primitives) this source is a complete self-contained assembly per wheel — a rim, a tyre and an already-modelled disc+caliper — so this mod ships none of mx5_lib's revolve()/radial_copies() geometry at all, only what the source authored. Each Wheel_NN in the pack sits on a display-tray placement (an arbitrary showcase rotation, not the wheel's real shape); orientation was recovered by measuring in that node's own local frame rather than raw import-world space, which resolves to a clean thin-axle/matched-diameter disc. Scaled uniformly so the tyre's own outer radius lands on TYRE_R (320.5mm), the same anchor every other wheel mod's tyre is built to, rather than RIM_R, since the source's tyre is real geometry here, not something built around a bare rim afterward.
mods.$materials: Deliberately NOT renamed into the MOD_* contract (materialContractExempt: true) — the source ships a small per-wheel baked texture (AO/highlight detail) that is very likely why it reads as a real wheel at under 1,000 triangles, and MOD_Rim's flat colour would replace that texture outright. wheel_01_metal/wheel_01_rubber keep their own name and texture and are mapped to a new 'static_textured' surfaceClasses.json entry that nothing tints — the Wheel finish picker has no effect on this mod, by design, confirmed with the user before building.
mods.$pilot: First of a 3-wheel pilot batch (WP01-WP03) proving a single parametrized Blender function (blender/mods/WP_wheelpack.py, build_wp(n, mod_id)) against the 30-wheel pack, rather than one bespoke script per wheel like WS01/WS02 needed. Later extended to 13 (WP04-WP13) once the pipeline held up.
mods.$bugs: Two rounds of the same bug. Round 1: WP01-WP03 shipped backwards (the back of the disc, the hub-mount side, not the finished face a spoke gap should reveal) — only surfaced from user feedback on the actual screenshots, since a numeric bbox/radius match can't tell front from back. Fixed with a blanket 180-degree flip applied to every wheel. Round 2: building WP04-WP13 immediately tripped a hard assertion showing Wheel_06, Wheel_07 and Wheel_13 measuring rim-and-brakes on the OPPOSITE local-frame side from every other wheel checked so far, which read as a second authoring convention worth respecting — so build_wp() was changed to flip only the wheels whose own measurement called for it, and shipped that way. It was WRONG: user inspection in the running app found 6, 7 and 13 backwards too. The measured asymmetry was noise, not a real second convention — a per-wheel heuristic that looks reasonable is not the same as one that is correct, and this one was guessing right 10 times out of 13. build_wp() now applies the same 180-degree flip to every wheel unconditionally, with no per-wheel branching at all.
